content:
watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major software update for Apple Watch, bringing a useful new feature that can extend your Apple Watch's battery life — the "Active Battery Extension Notification."

watchOS 27 can proactively extend your Apple Watch's battery life by disabling features you don't use.

watchOS 27 is on the way, bringing two new apps to Apple Watch, a useful tap gesture, a brand-new default home screen, three health-related upgrades, and more.

Another new feature in watchOS 27 is designed to improve your Apple Watch's battery life.

"Active Battery Extension Notification" is a new type of prompt you may see on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery extension notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected that you have several features you have never used, and disabling them can save battery life.

These features include various gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function that activates Siri, as well as "Start Workout" reminders and more.

Each of these features involves background processing, which puts a certain drain on battery life.

So in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you have never used these features, it will automatically disable them. The system will issue a "Battery Extension Notification" to inform you of the action and give you the option to keep them enabled.

If you regularly use these features, you will never see this prompt. Of course, you can always go into "Settings" to manually disable these features for longer battery life at any time.

Apple has not specified exactly how much additional battery life users can gain by disabling these features. But the energy savings are clearly worth the effort of building this new battery extension feature.

Have you tried Apple Watch's "Raise to Speak," gestures, or "Start Workout" reminders? Will you keep them enabled going forward? Let us know in the comments.
